heading: Carnia — a different country, a different collection, and one village missing
lead: Carnia is not in the Croatian collection, and finding what FamilySearch holds for it meant paging **all 3,483 of its collections**, because the collections API silently ignores its own text filter — a search for «Udine» returns Alabama. There is exactly one: **«Italy, Udine, Civil Registration (State Archive), 1806-1815, 1871-1911»**, collection 1939238, 1.26 million images.

findings.lab: The archive had half the dates
findings.text: This site has been describing the Udine holding as **«Stato civile (civil only) 1806–1815»** — the Napoleonic registers. The collection is **1806–1815 *and* 1871–1911**. The second half, sixty years of civil registration after Italian unification, has never been looked at here.

The province breaks down into **627 comuni**, and Ovaro is not one of them. Neither is Mione, Muina, Ovasta, Luint, Liariis, Chialina, Agrons nor Cludinico — every Val Degano name was checked.

**But Colza is there**, and Colza is a frazione of Ovaro. It holds a complete Napoleonic set for **1806–1812**: births, deaths, marriages, marriage banns and the indexes to all three. Twenty-five volumes.

**Whether Mione and Muina are written inside those volumes is a question the images can answer and the index cannot** — the record API's place filter is ignored, so it returns the same 2,201 people whatever place you give it. The volumes are linked below. It is a few minutes' reading to settle, and it has not been done yet.

findings.lab: Comeglians holds the allegati this archive already used
findings.text: Comeglians — the seat of the Gorto canton — carries the **marriage *allegati* for 1807 to 1815**, nine volumes. Those are the documents behind one of this archive's load-bearing findings: the *allegati* are what pushed the Mione family back to a **Giovanni Battista de' Franceschi already dead by 1789**. They were read from the Archivio di Stato di Udine; this is the same material, openable from a desk.

findings.lab: And a warning about the other two thousand
findings.text:
The collection indexes **2,201 people called Franceschi**. Of the first eleven hundred, sampled by the search's own ranking, **the Carnian communes barely appear — five entries in all.** The bulk are lowland Friulian families: Lauzzana and Colloredo di Monte Albano (209), Udine (129), Muzzana del Turgnano (114), Bertiolo (101), Magnano in Riviera (46).

**Most of the Franceschi in the Udine registers are not this family and are not from the mountains.** That is worth saying before anyone absorbs two thousand strangers into a Carnian pedigree.

note: Italy, Udine, Civil Registration (State Archive), collection 1939238, walked 14 September 2026. A link opens the volume's own first image; a free FamilySearch account is needed. These are civil registers, not parish books — the church registers of Carnia before 1806 are not on film anywhere and must be asked for at the parish, which is what this archive has said all along and still holds.
